sourceDate.text: 是歲；後漢隱帝乾祐三年十一月己丑，奉太后誥迎赟即位

claims.event: Liu Yun is formally selected to succeed, pending arrival. Jiuwudaishi 103 s0177-s0183 gives jichou, eleventh-month day 26, equivalent to 951-01-06 Julian / 951-01-11 proleptic Gregorian. This is selection, not completed accession.

sourceDate.text: 在位三年，崩時年二十；《舊五代史》卷一百三：乾祐三年十一月乙酉

dateContext.event: Yin's stated age at death is twenty sui. The death is on eleventh-month yiyou, day 22, equivalent to 951-01-02 Julian / 951-01-07 proleptic Gregorian. No birth year is derived.

sourceDate.text: 在位三年，崩時年二十；《舊五代史》卷一百三：乾祐三年十一月乙酉

dateContext.event: Yin dies on eleventh-month yiyou, day 22, equivalent to 951-01-02 Julian / 951-01-07 proleptic Gregorian, although the lunar-year label Qianyou 3 is conventionally AD 950.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝即位；在位三年；乾祐元年二月辛巳至乾祐三年十一月乙酉

claims.event: Yin's reign runs from the accession attested in 101 s0006-s0007 to the death in 103 s0150-s0152. The Chinese three-year statement counts the three Qianyou year labels; it is not three completed solar years.

people.descriptorSuggestion: Ruler of Han; son of Liu Zhiyuan

activeDateHints: on or before AD 947 (exact year unstated)

sourceDate.text: 降宋延渥；《宋史》宋偓傳：漢祖在晉陽，與偓結昏

claims.event: Song Yanwo participates in marriage arrangements with Gaozu's daughter while Gaozu is at Jinyang. The marriage is established by AD 947, not independently dated to the princess's fourth-month title.

people.descriptorSuggestion: Official and Father-in-law of Emperor Yin

activeDateHints: on or before AD 947 (exact year unstated)

sourceDate.text: 隱帝娶彥成女；《張彥成傳》：漢祖鎮北門，表為行軍司馬，以隱帝娶其女，特見親愛

claims.event: Zhang Yancheng personally serves as marching secretary under Gaozu's pre-imperial northern command. His daughter's marriage explains the favor but does not establish his full lifespan or an AD 948-950 activity interval.

sourceDate.text: 天福十二年；高祖建義於太原，遂停斂貸之議

claims.event: Gaozu raises his regime at Taiyuan, discusses army largess and accepts Li's advice to stop the levy. This is his own founding action, not activity inferred from his daughter's title.

sourceDate.text: 先帝；《舊五代史》卷一百一：乾祐元年正月二十七日，高祖崩，秘不發喪

dateContext.event: Gaozu's death precedes Yin's accession. The exact supplementary primary date is Qianyou 1 month 1 day 27, 948-03-10 Julian / 948-03-15 proleptic Gregorian. No new birth or age is inferred.

label.en: Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army
Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot
label.zh: 侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使

label.en: Military Commissioner of the Guide Army

sourceDate.text: 隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等；《通鑑》乾祐三年十一月乙亥告閻晉卿之前，丙子遂誅

claims.event: Li Ye participates in the plot presented to Li. Tongjian 289 places the final disclosure to Yan Jinqing on yihai (乙亥), eleventh-month day 12, and the murders on bingzi (丙子), day 13. This dates the immediate plotting episode, not every earlier grievance.

claims.action: rose in revolt at end of Han

claims.assessment: judged elevation of Lady Geng as empress too soon

sourceDate.text: 隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等；乾祐三年十一月乙亥告密、丙子誅邠之前

claims.event: Yang Bin is the living target of the immediate plot preceding the eleventh-month day-13 murders. His earlier objections to Geng's elevation and funeral are a separate temporal context.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝欲立耿夫人為後，邠以為太速；夫人卒，邠又止以后禮葬

claims.event: Yang Bin opposes Geng's proposed imperial elevation and later funeral. These acts follow Yin's AD 948 accession and precede Yang's murder on 950-12-24 Julian / 950-12-29 proleptic Gregorian. The interval bounds uncertainty about these acts, not continuous service throughout every year.

sourceDate.text: 南北軍遇於劉子陂；《通鑑》乾祐三年十一月癸未，翌日甲申交戰

claims.event: Guo Wei's army first encounters the imperial army at Liuzipo on guiwei, day 20: 950-12-31 Julian = 951-01-05 proleptic Gregorian. This is the encounter quoted in 104 s0018, not the next day's jia-shen battle. Under a Julian-year convention the old AD 950 was valid.

label.en: chief clerk of tribal and Han forces

activeDateHints: on or before AD 947 (exact year unstated)

sourceDate.text: 隱帝娶彥成女；《張彥成傳》：漢祖鎮北門，表為行軍司馬，以隱帝娶其女

claims.event: Zhang Yancheng's daughter was already Yin's wife during Gaozu's pre-imperial northern command. The marriage occurred by AD 947; its exact year and lower endpoint are unstated.

label.en: temporary attendance at court to hear government

sourceDate.text: 是歲；後漢隱帝乾祐三年冬十一月，赟未至，請太后權臨朝聽政

claims.event: Li issues governing orders after Guo Wei enters the capital and accepts temporary regency pending Liu Yun. Jiuwudaishi 103 s0177-s0185 associates the request with the eleventh-month jichou sequence (day 26); 110 s0184 and Tongjian 289 give day 27. Both are January AD 951 in Julian and proleptic Gregorian calendars; no exact regency day is asserted.

sourceDate.text: 高祖微時；及高祖領藩鎮；高祖建義於太原

claims.event: Li was taken as wife during Gaozu's obscure early life, before his provincial commands and his AD 947 imperial founding. This is only a conservative upper bound on that early episode, not a marriage in AD 947.

activeDateHints: Death date unknown; on or after the AD 947 living investiture. Huiyao, quoted in chapter 104, characterizes the Qin honor as posthumous and would imply death by it; Songshi narrates later maternal activity in the Song period. Neither account is selected; no exact death or common upper bound is known.

sourceDate.text: 降宋延渥；《宋史》宋偓傳：漢祖在晉陽，遣其子承訓至洛，奉書偓母，與偓結昏

dateContext.event: Yongning's marriage to Song Yanwo occurred by Gaozu's Jinyang phase and before the fourth-month 947 title record that already calls her 宋氏. The fourth-month date belongs to enfeoffment, not the wedding.

sourceDate.text: 乾祐二年十二月；《五代會要》作追封，《舊五代史》卷一百二壬午作進封

dateContext.event: Source-qualified Qin title history only, not a settled living or posthumous life event. The title/action fields preserve the cited Huiyao reading, quoted in 104 s0034, with textual-variant certainty; they must not be flattened into an unconditional posthumous fact. The parallel 102 annal reads advancement and dates renwu, month 12 day 13, to 950-01-04 Julian / 950-01-09 proleptic Gregorian. Matching the princess, Qin title, reign-year and month supports identifying the same honor across witnesses. Huiyao itself gives only a month spanning Western 949-950; its exact AD 950 event year is supplied by that explicit match, not by converting every day of the month to 950. The literal posthumous reading conditionally implies death by the honor; Songshi's Song-period maternal context supports the contrary later-life branch. Neither account is selected.

sourceDate.text: 乾祐二年十二月；《五代會要》作追封，《舊五代史》卷一百二壬午作進封

dateContext.event: Source-qualified Qin title history only, not a settled living or posthumous life event. The title/action fields preserve the cited Huiyao reading, quoted in 104 s0034, with textual-variant certainty; they must not be flattened into an unconditional posthumous fact. The parallel 102 annal reads advancement and dates renwu, month 12 day 13, to 950-01-04 Julian / 950-01-09 proleptic Gregorian. Matching the princess, Qin title, reign-year and month supports identifying the same honor across witnesses. Huiyao itself gives only a month spanning Western 949-950; its exact AD 950 event year is supplied by that explicit match, not by converting every day of the month to 950. The literal posthumous reading conditionally implies death by the honor; Songshi's Song-period maternal context supports the contrary later-life branch. Neither account is selected.

sourceDate.text: 天福十二年四月封；乾祐二年十二月追封；《五代會要》追封（本卷轉引）、《舊五代史》卷一百二進封、《宋史》卷二百四十二宋代隨母歸鎮及來賀長春節

dateContext.event: Actual death date unknown. Only the inclusive lower bound on or after the living Tianfu-12 fourth-month investiture, AD 947, is asserted. This is a contextual life-status inference from her own ordinary contemporary investiture, not an explicit source death date. Death later in 947 remains possible under this limited bound. Huiyao's posthumous reading conditionally implies death by the cross-witness AD 950 honor, whereas Songshi narrates later maternal activity in its Song-period context. Neither account is selected, and no shared upper endpoint, exact death, inferred birth, or continuous activity span is encoded.

sourceConflict.sharedEvidence: 099 s0136 is an ordinary contemporary investiture of the emperor's already-married daughter alongside his sons and nephew, not a funeral list; 104 s0034 identifies the same woman and date. Both conditional chronology branches admit this living AD 947 anchor. Her death cannot precede it, but no common upper terminus follows.
sourceConflict.sourceDependence: 104 s0034 explicitly quotes Wudai huiyao. Its 追封 is transmission of the same account, not an independent second historical vote. The annal and Songshi supply distinct accounts; no numerical vote or intersection of incompatible chronologies is attempted.

witnesses.source: Wudai huiyao, Siku edition, volume 2; quoted in 104 s0034
witnesses.conditionalChronology: If 追封 is read literally as posthumous, death occurred by the honor, not necessarily in its year. Huiyao gives Qianyou 2 month 12, which spans Western 949-950; the matching annal dates the same princess/title/month advancement to AD 950. Even without importing its day, this branch gives only death no later than AD 950. That upper bound is conditional and is not put in the common death container.

witnesses.reading: 永寧公主進封秦國長公主
witnesses.conditionalChronology: Dates advancement in AD 950 but does not itself explicitly date death or say posthumous.

witnesses.source: Songshi 242 s0496-s0502 and the checked web transcription's immediate Song-period context
witnesses.reading: 母漢永甯公主。后幼時隨母入見，周太祖賜冠帔。時偓任華州節度，后隨母歸鎮。孝明后崩，復隨母來賀長春節。
witnesses.conditionalChronology: The retrospective name 周太祖 alone does not prove that the earlier audience followed his accession; its reign placement is contextual, not an explicit date. Independently, the same paragraph narrates maternal accompaniment in the Song period: return to Wo's Huazhou command following the web text's 乾德五年 notice, and a visit for Changchun festival after Xiaoming's death. On the text's natural continuous maternal reference these concern the mother just identified as Han Princess Yongning and support later life incompatible with death by AD 950. No checked passage announces a switch to a stepmother. This remains a source-qualified branch, not an exact maternal event/death year or an assertion that every mother reference must always be biological.

sourceConflict.resolution: No witness selected or emended. Only the independently supported AD 947 lower bound is encoded. The incompatible death-by-honor and later-life implications remain explicitly conditional. Unknown exact death and unselected witness priority do not invalidate this narrower supported assertion.

sourceDate.text: 夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之；楊邠在乾祐三年十一月十三日被誅之前

dateContext.event: Geng dies before Yang Bin blocks her imperial funeral, therefore before his murder on 950-12-24 Julian / 950-12-29 proleptic Gregorian. This is a one-sided upper bound, not a death in AD 950.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝欲立耿夫人為後，邠以為太速；在隱帝即位之後、夫人卒之前

claims.event: Geng is alive when Yin proposes her elevation to empress. This particular proposal follows his AD 948 accession and precedes her death and Yang Bin's AD 950 murder. The interval does not date the onset or whole duration of imperial favor.

units.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也。
units.en: Empress Li, consort of Later Han Gaozu, came from Jinyang.
units.literal: Empress Li of Gaozu was a native of Jinyang.

units.zh: 高祖微時，嘗牧馬於晉陽別墅，因夜入其家，劫而取之。
units.en: While Liu Zhiyuan was still a nobody, he tended horses at a Jinyang country house, slipped in one night, and carried her off.
units.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure, he once pastured horses at a villa outside Jinyang, and because of that entered her house by night, seized her, and took her away.

units.zh: 及高祖領藩鎮，累封魏國夫人。
units.en: Once he held a frontier command she rose step by step to Lady of Wei.
units.literal: When Gaozu took charge of a military province, she was repeatedly ennobled as lady of Wei.

units.zh: 高祖建義於太原，欲行頒賚於軍士，以公帑不足，議率井邑，助成其事。
units.en: At Taiyuan he meant to pay the troops but the state coffers ran dry, so his council weighed a levy on town and countryside to fund the bonuses.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan and wished to distribute largess among the soldiers, because the public treasury was insufficient they deliberated levying the towns and villages to help accomplish the matter.

units.zh: 後聞而諫曰：「自晉高祖建義，及國家興運，雖出於天意，亦土地人民福力同致耳，未能惠其眾而欲奪其財，非新天子恤隱之理也。
units.en: The empress heard of it and remonstrated, saying, "From the time Jin Gaozu raised the righteous cause down to our dynasty's rise to fortune, although it came from Heaven's will, it was also because the blessing-power of the land and the people arrived together; to fail to show kindness to the multitude yet wish to strip their wealth is not the way a new Son of Heaven should pity the distressed.
units.literal: The empress heard of it and remonstrated, saying, "From the time Jin Gaozu raised the righteous cause down to our dynasty's rise to fortune, although it came from Heaven's will, it was also because the blessing-power of the land and the people arrived together; to fail to show kindness to the multitude yet wish to strip their wealth is not the way a new Son of Heaven should pity the distressed.

units.zh: 今後宮所積，宜悉以散之，設使不厚，人無怨言。」
units.en: Empty the palace hoards first; even thin gifts will silence grumbling."
units.literal: What the rear palace has stored up ought all to be scattered among them; even if the gifts are not lavish, the people will have no cause for complaint."

units.zh: 高祖改容曰：「敬聞命矣。」
units.en: The emperor colored and said, "Your counsel is taken."
units.literal: Gaozu changed countenance and said, "I respectfully accept the command."

units.zh: 遂停斂貸之議。
units.en: He dropped the plan for forced loans.
units.literal: Thereupon he stopped the proposal to collect loans.

units.zh: 後傾內府以助之，中外聞者，無不感悅。
units.en: She then opened the privy purse to make up the sum, and word of it gladdened the whole court and camp.
units.literal: Later she poured out the inner treasury to assist it; those who heard of it within and without were all moved and pleased.

units.zh: 天福十二年，冊為皇后。
units.en: In Tianfu 12 she received the empress's seals.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianfu she was invested as empress.

units.zh: 隱帝即位，尊為皇太后。
units.en: When Emperor Yin succeeded she became empress dowager.
units.literal: When the Yin Emperor ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下疑有闕文。
units.en: Editor's note: the passage below is likely corrupt.
units.literal: Annotation: the text that follows is probably defective.

units.zh: 據《通鑒》云：隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等，議既定，入白太后，太后曰：「茲事何可輕發，更宜與宰相議之。」
units.en: The 《Zizhi tongjian》 records that Emperor Yin and Li Ye resolved to kill Yang Bin; when they told the dowager she said, "Do not rush this; take it to the chief ministers first."
units.literal: According to the 《Zizhi tongjian》: the Yin Emperor plotted with Li Ye and others to execute Yang Bin and the rest; when the plan was settled they entered to report to the empress dowager, and the empress dowager said, "How can such a matter be lightly set in motion? You should further discuss it with the chief ministers."

units.zh: 業時在旁曰：「先帝嘗言，朝廷大事不可謀及書生，懦怯誤人。」
units.en: Li Ye at her elbow said, "The late emperor warned never to plot great matters with pedants—they only breed cowardice."
units.literal: Ye, who was at the side at the time, said, "The late emperor once said that great affairs of the court must not be plotted with bookish men—timidity misleads men."

units.zh: 太后復以為言，帝忿曰：「國家之事，非閨門所知。」
units.en: She pressed again; the emperor snapped, "State business is no concern of women's quarters."
units.literal: The empress dowager repeated her words, and the emperor angrily said, "Affairs of the state are not for the inner chambers to know."

units.zh: 拂衣而出。
units.en: He flung aside his robe and left.
units.literal: He shook out his sleeves and went out.

units.zh: 又云：南北軍遇於劉子陂，帝欲自出勞軍，太后曰：「郭威吾家故舊，非死亡切身，何以至此！
units.en: The same work adds: at Liuzipo the young ruler meant to ride out to hearten the lines; the dowager cried, "Guo Wei is family to us—would he rebel without mortal cause!
units.literal: It also says: when the northern and southern armies met at Liuzipo, the emperor wished to go out himself to encourage the troops, and the empress dowager said, "Guo Wei is an old friend of our house—unless death pressed close, how could matters come to this!

units.zh: 但按兵守城，飛詔諭之，觀其志趣，必有辭理，則君臣之禮尚全，慎勿輕出。」
units.en: Keep the gates shut, send him a clear edict, and read his answer; lord and minister may yet mend their breach—do not rashly ride forth."
units.literal: Only hold the troops and guard the city, fly an edict to instruct him, observe his intentions—surely there will be words of reason, and then the rites between lord and minister can still remain whole; be careful not to go out lightly."

units.zh: 帝不從。）〉
units.en: The young ruler brushed aside her warning. (End of editorial note.)〉
units.literal: The emperor did not comply. (End of editorial note.)〉

units.zh: 周太祖入京，凡軍國大事，皆請後發教令以行之。
units.en: After Guo Wei took the capital he still had her issue the orders that ran the realm.
units.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, for every great affair of army and state he all asked the empress dowager to issue instructional orders to carry them out.

units.zh: 是歲，議立徐州節度使赟為帝，以迎奉未至，周太祖乃率群臣拜章，請後權臨朝聽政，後於是稱誥焉。
units.en: That year they planned to enthrone Liu Yun, the Xuzhou military commissioner; because the welcoming escort had not yet arrived, Guo Wei led the ministers to memorialize the dowager to hold court temporarily as regent, and she thereupon spoke in edict form.
units.literal: That year they deliberated establishing the Xuzhou military commissioner Yun as emperor; because the welcoming escort had not yet arrived, Zhou Taizu thereupon led the host of ministers to submit a memorial and asked the empress dowager temporarily to attend court and hear government, and the empress dowager thereupon spoke in the manner of an edict.

units.zh: 及周太祖為六軍推戴，上章具述其事，且言願事後為慈母。
units.en: When the Six Armies raised Guo Wei, his memorial laid out every step and vowed to honor her as a mother.
units.literal: When Zhou Taizu was acclaimed by the Six Armies, he submitted a memorial setting forth the affair in detail and moreover said he wished to serve the empress dowager as a kind mother.

units.zh: 後下誥答曰：「侍中功烈崇高，德聲昭著，翦除禍亂，安定乾坤，謳歌有歸，歷數攸屬，所以軍民推戴，億兆同歡。
units.en: "Your merit towers high and your virtuous name shines bright; you have cut away turmoil and steadied heaven and earth. Song and acclaim have found their lord, the mandate is rightly yours, and army and people together rejoice.
units.literal: The empress dowager issued an answering edict saying, "The attendant-in-chief's merit and achievement are lofty, his virtuous name shines bright; he has cut away calamity and disorder and stabilized heaven and earth; songs of praise have a proper object, the celestial succession belongs where it ought—therefore army and people have pushed him forward and a hundred million share the joy.

units.zh: 老身未終殘年，屬茲多難，惟以衰朽，托於始終。
units.en: I am old and worn, yet live through this storm; I can only lean on you to the end.
units.literal: I, old woman, have not yet finished my remaining years, yet meet these many hardships; I can only, in my decay, entrust myself from beginning to end.

units.zh: 載省來箋，如母見待，感念深意，涕泗橫流」云。
units.en: Your words treat me as a mother might be treated—I weep as I read them."
units.literal: Having read your letter, you treat me as a mother; I am moved by the deep meaning and tears and mucus stream across my face," and so on.

units.zh: 仍出戎衣、玉帶以賜周太祖。
units.en: She sent him a field robe and a jade belt as gifts.
units.literal: She moreover presented a campaign robe and jade belt to bestow on Zhou Taizu.

units.zh: 周太祖即位，上尊號曰德聖皇太后，居於太平宮。
units.en: Once Guo Wei took the throne he styled her the Virtuous and Sagely Empress Dowager and housed her at Taiping Palace.
units.literal: When Zhou Taizu ascended the throne, he honored her with the title Virtuous and Sagely Empress Dowager and she dwelt at the Palace of Great Peace.

units.zh: 周顯德元年春薨。
units.en: She died in the spring of Zhou Xiande 1.
units.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande of Zhou she died.

units.zh: 〈（案：隱帝未立皇后，據薛史《張彥成傳》云：隱帝娶彥成女。
units.en: Editor's note: Yin never crowned a queen; the Old History biography of Zhang Yancheng says he wed Zhang Yancheng's daughter.
units.literal: Annotation: Emperor Yin never invested an empress; according to the 《Zhang Yancheng zhuan》 in Xue's history, Yin married Yancheng's daughter.

units.zh: 《楊邠傳》云：隱帝所愛耿夫人，欲立為後，邠以為太速，夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之。
units.en: The 《Yang Bin zhuan》 adds that Yin doted on Lady Geng and wanted her as empress; Yang Bin called it premature. When she died Yin demanded an empress's funeral, and Yang Bin blocked that too.
units.literal: The 《Yang Bin zhuan》 states: the Lady Geng whom Yin favored he wished to establish as empress, but Bin thought it too soon; when the lady died Yin wished to bury her with empress rites, and Bin again stopped him.

units.zh: 蓋隱帝在位三年，崩時年二十，故未及冊立皇后也。
units.en: He ruled barely three years and died at twenty, so he never crowned a queen.
units.literal: Probably because Yin reigned only three years and was twenty sui when he perished, therefore he had not yet reached the investiture of an empress.

units.zh: 又，《五代會要》載：漢高祖長女永寧公主，降宋延渥，天福十二年四月封，至乾祐二年十二月，追封秦國長公主。）〉
units.en: The 《Wudai hui yao》 also notes Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Yongning, wed Song Yanwo, was titled in Tianfu 12, and was posthumously raised to princess of Qin in Qianyou 2. (End of editorial note.)〉
units.literal: Moreover, the 《Wudai hui yao》 records: Han Gaozu's eldest daughter, the Princess of Yongning, was married to Song Yanwo; she was enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 12, and in the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou was posthumously advanced to elder princess of Qin. (End of editorial note.)〉

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 是日，定州孫方簡、徐州劉赟並加同平章事，以利州節度使宋延渥為滑州節度使。
units.en: That day, Sun Fangjian of Ding Prefecture and Liu Yun of Xuzhou were both made Grand Councilors, and the Lizhou military governor Song Yanwo was appointed military governor of Hua Prefecture.
units.literal: That day, Ding Prefecture Sun Fangjian and Xuzhou Liu Yun were both made Grand Councilors; the Lizhou military governor Song Yanwo was made military governor of Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 漢主劉知遠殂，子承祐立。
units.en: Han ruler Liu Zhiyuan died, and his son Chengyou succeeded him.
units.literal: Han ruler Liu Zhiyuan died, and his son Chengyou succeeded.

units.zh: 漢郭威弒其主自立，國號周，遣朱憲來告。
units.en: Guo Wei of Han murdered his sovereign and declared himself emperor under the state name Zhou, then sent Zhu Xian to announce it.
units.literal: Guo Wei of Han murdered his lord and declared himself emperor; his state name was Zhou, and he sent Zhu Xian to report it.

units.zh: 甲辰，相州張彥成移鎮鄧州，折從阮移鎮滑州，李筠移鎮相州。
units.en: On jiachen day, Zhang Yancheng transferred from Xiang to Deng, Zhe Congruan to Hua, and Li Jun to Xiang.
units.literal: On the day jiachen, Zhang Yancheng of Xiang prefecture was transferred to Deng prefecture, Zhe Congruan was transferred to Hua prefecture, and Li Jun was transferred to Xiang prefecture.

units.zh: 丙辰，以秘書監呂琦為禮部侍郎，歸德軍節度使趙在禮改天平軍節度使，昭義軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候杜重威改忠武軍節度使，忠武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠改歸德軍節度使，前河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使侯益改昭義軍節度使。
units.en: On bingchen Lü Qi, palace library director, became vice minister of rites; Zhao Zaili of Guide became Tianping military commissioner; Du Chongwei of Zhaoyi became Zhongwu military commissioner; Liu Zhiyuan of Zhongwu became Guide military commissioner; and Hou Yi, former Heyang commissioner, became Zhaoyi military commissioner.
units.literal: On bingchen, Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; Zhao Zaili, Military Commissioner of the Guide Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army; Hou Yi, former Military Commissioner of Heyang and Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 漢末李業等作亂，後與貴妃張氏及諸皇族同日遇禍。
units.en: At the end of Han, when Li Ye and others rose in revolt, she, Honored Consort Zhang, and the imperial kin were killed on the same day.
units.literal: At the end of Han, Li Ye and others made trouble; the lady with Honored Consort Zhang and the imperial kin met disaster on the same day.

units.zh: 辛亥，宰臣竇貞固加守司徒，蘇逢吉加守司空，蘇禹珪加左僕射，楊邠加右僕射，依前兼樞密使。
units.en: On xinhai, chief minister Dou Zhengu was given Acting Minister of Education, Su Fengji Acting Minister of Works, Su Yugui Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Yang Bin Right Vice Director, all continuing as before with concurrent Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner.
units.literal: On xinhai, chief minister Dou Zhengu was given Acting Minister of Education; Su Fengji Acting Minister of Works; Su Yugui Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Yang Bin Right Vice Director, all continuing as before with concurrent Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner.

units.zh: 以蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威為權樞密使、檢校司徒；
units.en: Guo Wei was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;
units.literal: Guo Wei, chief clerk of tribal and Han forces, was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;

units.zh: 高祖皇后李氏
units.en: Empress Li, wife of Gaozu of Later Han
units.literal: Gaozu's Empress, the Li clan

units.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也，其父為農。
units.en: Empress Li of Gaozu was a native of Jinyang; her father was a farmer.
units.literal: Empress Li, wife of Gaozu, was from Jinyang; her father was a farmer.

units.zh: 高祖即位，立為皇后。
units.en: When Gaozu ascended, she was made empress.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, she was installed as empress.

units.zh: 高祖已貴，封魏國夫人，生隱帝。
units.en: When Gaozu rose to power, she was made Lady of Wei and bore the Hidden Emperor.
units.literal: After Gaozu had risen high, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei and bore the Hidden Emperor.

units.zh: 高祖崩，隱帝冊尊為皇太后。
units.en: After Gaozu's death, the Hidden Emperor made her empress dowager.
units.literal: When Gaozu died, the Hidden Emperor enfeoffed and honored her as empress dowager.

units.zh: 於是遷后於太平宮，上尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
units.en: She was moved to Taiping Palace and titled Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
units.literal: Thereupon she was moved to the Taiping Palace and honored as Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.

units.zh: 已而議立湘陰公赟為天子，赟未至，太祖乃請太后臨朝。
units.en: They meant to make the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, emperor; before he arrived, Guo Wei had the dowager hold court.
units.literal: Soon they deliberated enthroning the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, as Son of Heaven; before Yun arrived, Taizu asked the empress dowager to hold court.

units.zh: 顯德元年春崩。
units.en: She died in spring of Xiande 1.
units.literal: In spring of the first year of Xiande she died.

units.zh: 后諫曰：「方今起事，號為義兵，民未知惠而先奪其財，殆非新天子所以救民之意也。
units.en: She admonished him: "We call this a righteous rising, yet we seize people's goods before they know our kindness—is that how a new emperor saves his people?
units.literal: The empress admonished, saying: "Now in raising the affair we call ourselves righteous troops; the people have not yet known kindness when we first seize their goods—this is scarcely what a new Son of Heaven intends in saving the people.

units.zh: 今後宮所有，請悉出之，雖其不足，士亦不以為怨也。」
units.en: Take everything the inner palace holds; even if it is not enough, the soldiers will not resent it."
units.literal: What the inner palace now holds, please bring it all forth; though it be insufficient, the soldiers will not regard it as cause for resentment."

units.zh: 高祖為改容謝之。
units.en: Gaozu softened and thanked her.
units.literal: Gaozu changed expression and thanked her.

units.zh: 太后曰：「此大事也，當與宰相議之。」
units.en: She said: “This is grave—it must go to the chief ministers.”
units.literal: The empress dowager said: “This is a great affair—it should be discussed with the chief ministers.”

units.zh: 邠等死，周太祖起兵向京師，慕容彥超敗於劉子陂，帝欲出自臨兵，太后止之曰：「郭威本吾家人，非其危疑，何肯至此！
units.en: After their deaths, Taizu of Zhou marched on the capital; Murong Yanchao was defeated at Liuzipo; the emperor meant to take the field himself; the dowager stopped him: “Guo Wei was originally one of our household—had he not been driven to doubt, how would he have come to this!
units.literal: When Bin and the others were dead, Taizu of Zhou raised troops toward the capital; Murong Yanchao was defeated at Liuzipo; the emperor wished to go out in person to command the army; the empress dowager stopped him, saying: “Guo Wei was originally one of our household—had he not been driven to doubt, how would he have come to this!

units.zh: 今若按兵無動，以詔諭威，威必有說，則君臣之際，庶幾尚全。」
units.en: Hold your troops, send him an edict of explanation—he will answer, and lord and minister may yet be whole.”
units.literal: Now if you hold the army still and do not move, and with an edict explain matters to Wei, Wei will surely have something to say—then between lord and minister perhaps something may still be preserved.”

units.zh: 太祖請事太后為母，太后誥曰：「侍中功烈崇高，德聲昭著，剪除禍亂，安定邦家，謳歌有歸，歷數攸屬，所以軍民推戴，億兆同歡。
units.en: He asked to honor her as mother; her edict read: “The attendant-in-chief’s merit towers, his virtue shines; he has ended chaos and steadied the realm—the army and people have chosen him, and all rejoice.
units.literal: Taizu asked to treat the empress dowager as his mother; the dowager’s edict said: “The attendant-in-chief’s merit is lofty, his virtue renowned; he has cut away calamity and settled the realm; songs of praise have a target, the mandate has found its seat—therefore the army and people have pushed him forward, the millions rejoice together.

units.zh: 老身未終殘年，屬此多難，唯以衰朽，托於始終。
units.en: I have not outlived my years, yet meet such troubles; in my weakness I trust myself to the end.
units.literal: I have not finished my declining years, yet meet such many troubles; only in my decay do I entrust myself to the end.

units.zh: 載省來箋，如母見待，感認深意，涕泗橫流。」
units.en: Your letter treats me as a mother—I am moved to tears.”
units.literal: Reading your letter, you treat me as a mother—I feel the deep meaning and my tears stream.”

units.zh: 而宗室河東節度使崇等在者四人，乃為太后誥曰：「河東節度使崇，許州節度使信，皆高祖之弟，徐州節度使赟，開封尹承勳，皆高祖之子，文武百辟，其擇嗣君以承天統。」
units.en: Four of the Liu clan remained; the dowager's edict read: "Chong of Hedong, Xin of Xu, Yun of Xuzhou, and Chengxun of Kaifeng—brothers and sons of Gaozu—and bade the court choose an heir."
units.literal: Among the imperial clan, Chong of Hedong and the others, four were present; an edict was issued for the dowager: “Chong, military governor of Hedong, and Xin, military governor of Xu—both Gaozu’s younger brothers; Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, and Chengxun, metropolitan governor of Kaifeng—both Gaozu’s sons: civil and military officials, choose an heir to receive Heaven’s succession.

units.zh: 太后以承勳久病，不任為嗣。
units.en: She said Chengxun was too ill.
units.literal: The empress dowager said Chengxun had long been ill and could not bear the succession.

units.zh: 太祖已監國，太后乃下誥曰：「此者樞密使郭威，誌安宗社，議立長君，以徐州節度使赟高祖近親，立為漢嗣，乃自藩鎮召赴京師。
units.en: As regent, the dowager issued an edict: "Guo Wei had meant to enthrone an elder lord; Yun, Gaozu's kin, was chosen and summoned from Xuzhou.
units.literal: Taizu was already regent; the empress dowager then issued an edict: “Here the commissioner Guo Wei, intent on settling the altars, deliberated enthroning the elder lord; because Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, was Gaozu’s close kin, he was made Han heir and summoned from his command to the capital.

units.zh: 雖誥命已行，而軍情不附，天道在北，人心靡東。
units.en: The decree went out, but the army would not follow; Heaven favored the north, not the east.
units.literal: Though the decree had gone forth, the army's heart did not adhere; Heaven's way lay in the north, men's hearts not in the east.

units.zh: 適當改卜之初，俾膺分土之命，赟可降授開府儀同三司，檢校太師、上柱國，封湘陰公。」
units.en: Yun was demoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, acting Grand Preceptor, supreme pillar of state, and made Duke of Xiangyin.”
units.literal: At the beginning of changing the choice, let him receive a fief’s command: Yun may be demoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, acting Grand Preceptor, supreme pillar of state, and enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyin.”

units.zh: 開運四年，高祖起兵太原，賞軍士，帑藏不足充，欲斂於民。
units.en: In Kaiyun 4, Gaozu rebelled at Taiyuan and meant to reward his troops, but the treasury fell short and he planned to levy the people.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyun, Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan and rewarded the soldiers; the treasury was insufficient, and he wished to levy upon the people.

units.zh: 帝年少，數與小人郭允明、後贊、李業等遊戲宮中，後數切責之。
units.en: As a youth the emperor often caroused in the palace with Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, Li Ye, and other low companions; the empress scolded him again and again.
units.literal: When the emperor was young he often played in the palace with petty men Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, Li Ye, and others; the empress repeatedly rebuked him sternly.

units.zh: 帝曰：「國家之事，外有朝廷，非太后所宜言也。」
units.en: He said: “Government belongs to the court outside—the empress dowager should not meddle.”
units.literal: The emperor said: “State affairs are handled outside, with the court—this is not what the empress dowager should speak of.”

units.zh: 初，帝與允明等謀誅楊邠、史弘肇等，議已定，入白太后。
units.en: When he and Yunming had settled on killing Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the others, he told the empress dowager.
units.literal: At first, when the emperor and Yunming and the others plotted to execute Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest, and the plan was settled, he entered to tell the empress dowager.

units.zh: 太后深以為不可，帝拂衣而去，曰：「何必謀於閨門！」
units.en: She strongly objected; he flung off and left, saying: “Must we take counsel only from the inner quarters!”
units.literal: The empress dowager deeply thought this wrong; the emperor shook out his robes and left, saying: “Why must we plot within the women’s quarters!”

units.zh: 周太祖入京師，舉事皆稱太后誥。
units.en: When Guo Wei entered the capital, he acted in the dowager’s name.
units.literal: When Taizu of Zhou entered the capital, in all affairs he invoked the empress dowager’s edicts.

units.zh: 太祖意色皆沮，以謂漢大臣未有推立己意，又難於自立，因白漢太后擇立漢嗣。
units.en: Guo Wei’s face fell; no Han minister meant to make him emperor; he asked the dowager to choose a Han heir.
units.literal: Taizu’s expression and color were both dejected; he thought Han ministers had no intent to raise him; it was hard to raise himself; he therefore told Han’s empress dowager to choose a Han heir.

units.zh: 於是周太祖與王峻入見太后，言：「開封尹承勳，高祖皇帝之子，宜立。」
units.en: Guo Wei and Wang Jun told the dowager: “Chengxun, Gaozu’s son, should reign.”
units.literal: Thereupon Taizu of Zhou and Wang Jun entered to see the empress dowager, saying: “Chengxun, Kaifeng metropolitan governor, is Gaozu’s son—he should be enthroned.”

units.zh: 太祖與群臣請見承勳視起居，太后命以臥榻舁承勳出見群臣，群臣視之信然，乃共奏曰：「徐州節度使赟，高祖愛之，以為子，宜立為嗣。」
units.en: They asked to see Chengxun; he was borne out on a couch; seeing him truly ill, they memorialized: "Yun, whom Gaozu had adopted, should be enthroned as heir."
units.literal: Taizu and the ministers asked to see Chengxun to observe his rising and resting; the empress dowager ordered him carried out on a couch to meet the ministers; the ministers saw it was true; they jointly memorialized: “Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, whom Gaozu loved and made his son, should be enthroned as heir.”

units.zh: 道見赟，傳太后意召之。
units.en: He told Yun the dowager summoned him.
units.literal: When Dao saw Yun he conveyed the empress dowager’s intent to summon him.

units.zh: 太祖以書召道先歸，留其副趙上交、王度奉赟入朝太后。
units.en: Guo Wei recalled Dao first and left Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to bring Yun to court.
units.literal: Taizu by letter summoned Dao to return first and left his deputies Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to escort Yun into court to the empress dowager.
